title: Partial-stream JSON-mode recovery and tolerant constrained-decoder tests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Expand the structured-output test harness to validate recovery semantics when streaming JSON-mode payloads are fragmented or partially malformed, and to verify a new 'tolerant constrained-decoder' mode that attempts best-effort reconstruction of fields without silently dropping required keys.

Background: We currently have strict JSON-mode enforcement tests and constrained-decoding suites, but most tests assume whole-response delivery. In production streaming (server-sent tokens / chunked responses) we observe edge cases where network truncation, interleaved tool-calls, or streaming artifacts produce: truncated JSON, trailing commas, or partial arrays across chunks. Consumers using older compatibility layers (v1 clients) expect either a full rejection or a workable fallback object; newer clients (v2) prefer a deterministic error token + structured partial payload.

Scope: Build automated tests and fixtures that simulate realistic streaming fragmentation patterns and evaluate two runtime behaviours: 1) strict-reject: current behavior that fails schema validation and emits an error; 2) tolerant-reconstruct: new experimental constrained-decoder option that applies a deterministic reconstruction policy (prefix completion, array padding with sentinel, required-key placeholders) and emits a schema-adherence score in diagnostic metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add 24 unique test cases covering: chunk boundary splits inside strings, arrays split across chunks, KV-cache-inserted tokens mid-json, tool-call delimiters within object bodies, and trailing stream truncation.
- Each test exercises both strict-reject and tolerant-reconstruct modes and records: validation result, reconstructed payload (if any), diagnostics trace, and time-to-validate.
- Diagnostics format matches console and API trace expectations (trace_id linkable to QA dashboard).
- Tests run in CI (integration) without flaky failures >1% across 50 runs.
- Add compatibility verification that v1 client deserializers get a defined fallback object when tolerant-reconstruct is enabled (documented behavior).

Test plan summary:
1) Fixtures: generate tokenized streams from canonical model outputs, then synthesize fragmentation by injecting chunk boundaries at deterministic offsets and randomized offsets. Save fixtures in test-fixtures/streaming/partial-*.jsonl (link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/streaming-fixtures/partial-stream-fixtures).
2) Harness: extend structured-output-test-runner to support streaming input and to toggle decoder modes via test config flags.
3) Metrics: add assertions for schema errors count, reconstruction accuracy (field-level F1), and diagnostic payload presence. Wire metrics to QA dashboard (https://dash.redwood.com/d/struct-out/stream-frag).
4) Backcompat tests: run baseline v1 client deserialization (JavaScript/Go) against reconstructed outputs and confirm client-visible shape.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement production rollout of tolerant-reconstruct; it only tests and specifies behavior. Rollout/feature-flag will be separate (ENG-43012).
- No UI changes to Console are included here; console integration tracked in PM-518.

Outcomes and risk mitigation:
- If tolerant-reconstruct shows acceptable reconstruction accuracy and low false-positives, we will propose adding it behind a runtime flag for canary testing.
- To avoid silent data corruption, reconstructed payloads MUST include a diagnostics.topology field with reconstruction hints; tests assert presence.
